issues.detail: The Greek 'ειδοτας υμας' (knowing you) is a participle modifying the subject (I), but the Vietnamese translation 'là người đã biết điều này' (who already knew this) treats it as a relative clause describing 'anh em' (you). The Greek implies 'I want to remind you, knowing you [already]...', whereas the Vietnamese says 'I want to remind you, who [already] know...'
The Greek 'απαξ' (once/at one time) is present but the Vietnamese 'một lần rồi' is slightly shifted in focus; however, the primary issue is the grammatical role of the participle.
